history.dynasty: Badami Chalukya (initial structure); later additions under the Vijayanagara Empire; a 10th-century local Nanda-king legend gives the place its name
history.period: Origins traced to the 7th century (Badami Chalukya); major additions in the 10th and 15th centuries; inscriptions speak of repeated repairs
history.summary: NOTE: CSV town 'Kurnool' is imprecise - the temple is at Mahanandi village in Nandyal district (carved out of Kurnool in 2022), about 21 km from Nandyal city. Mahanandi is the nucleus of the Nava Nandis, nine Nandi shrines within about 15 km: Mahanandi, Sivanandi, Vinayakanandi, Somanandi, Prathamanandi, Garudanandi, Suryanandi, Krishnanandi (Vishnunandi) and Naganandi. It is one of India's oldest Shaivite centres - over 1,500 years old. Its most famous feature is the crystal-clear Pushkarini: spring water flows from beneath the garbhagriha into a 60-foot tank with a central mandapam, staying at a constant level and running all year; devotees are unusually permitted to touch the Swayambhu linga and the water around it. The central gopuram is in the Badami Chalukyan style and the later structures in Vijayanagara style. Legend says the local Nanda kings of the 10th century built temples here and worshipped their ancestral deity the Nandi, hence 'Mahanandi' (the great Nandi).

name: Mahanandi Temple
town_description: Mahanandi is a village at the eastern foothills of the Nallamala forest range in Nandyal district, about 21 km from Nandyal city. Surrounded by forests, it is a pilgrimage centre for the Nava Nandi temples; the AP Tourism Haritha Hotel and several lodges serve visitors. The surrounding region is agricultural, partly irrigated by the temple spring's outflow (said to irrigate over 2,000 acres).

travel.railway: Nandyal Railway Station, about 19-21 km away; well connected to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Vijayawada and Chennai.
travel.road: Mahanandi is well connected by bus with Nandyal (21 km) and Srisailam; state buses also run from Cuddapah, Hyderabad, Tirupati, Nellore, Chennai and Kurnool.
